source: a16z Podcast — AI demand outrunning compute supply; frontier-lab revenue is self-determined, reinvestment math, not necessarily winner-take-all
summary: SpaceX is a multi-trillion dollar opportunity even without orbital compute, via Starlink mobile (wireless + broadband ~$2T TAM), rapidly growing AI/AR revenue base, and cloud business
summary_extended: Baker argues that SpaceX is likely to become the first $20+ trillion dollar company, driven by multiple compounding revenue streams that extend well beyond its launch business. The core thesis rests on Starlink mobile addressing an $800–900B wireless and broadband market within a ~$2T total addressable market, combined with rapidly growing X advertising revenue (for which Atreides claims proprietary telemetry data) and an emerging AI/AR product suite including Grok-based applications. Baker draws an explicit analogy to Google's strategy of bundling cloud infrastructure with advertising, envisioning a Starlink/Grok/X-advertising bundle as a similarly self-reinforcing ecosystem. Even in a bear case where SpaceX fails to execute on first-party AI applications, Baker contends the pure infrastructure business — satellite broadband, orbital compute, launch — remains a multi-trillion dollar asset, making the downside case still compelling.
detail: Starlink mobile addresses ~$800-900B wireless + broadband market, total ~$2T addressable. X ads are growing (Atreides has telemetry). Baker envisions a Starlink/Grockbot/X-advertising bundle analogous to Google bundling cloud with ads. Even in a scenario where SpaceX fumbles first-party AI applications, it remains a massive infrastructure business. Baker implies SpaceX is the first candidate for a $20T+ company.
